summary: The truth-file switch is internally consistent, and the revised paper numbers match the regenerated tables. Two major issues remain: the paper treats a highly selected FamilySearch-linked sample as independent validation without establishing that independence, and the replication gate succeeds despite leaving 37 new empirical numbers unchecked. The package documentation also retains obsolete results and an obsolete one-sided definition of contradiction.

findings.title: The validation standard is selected on prior successful linkage and vital-data coverage, yet the paper presents it as independent evidence
findings.what_the_code_does: The truth sample first intersects the pre-existing 1930 and 1940 FamilySearch-profile crosswalks using `merge 1:1 unique_ID ... keep(3)`, then retains only profiles with observed birth and death dates through `keep if birthyr!=. & deathyr!=. & birthmon!=. & deathmon!=. & _merge==3 ...`. The code therefore evaluates links only among people already linked successfully in both censuses and covered by the profile/vital-date data; it neither constructs nor audits those upstream crosswalk links. The paper instead calls this an “independent set of high-quality genealogical links” and uses it to distinguish genuine from spurious recovery.
findings.why_it_matters: Name quality can affect inclusion in the FamilySearch crosswalk itself. If people with clear, common, or internally consistent names are more likely to enter the standard, verified counts, recall, and contradicted-link shares need not generalize to the difficult records the model targets. The direction of the reported within-standard comparisons may still be informative, but the strong independence and genuine-recovery language is not established by the supplied code.
findings.how_to_check: Obtain the construction documentation for `unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1930/1940.dta` and tabulate truth-set inclusion by Ancestry–FamilySearch disagreement, name commonness, race, nativity, and baseline linkage status. Also compare old/new link outcomes separately for records with neither, one, or both census identifiers represented in the truth set.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe exactly how the two upstream profile-to-census crosswalks were created and whether census names entered those links. Recast the result as validation within a selected FamilySearch-linked subset unless independence can be demonstrated, and report truth-set coverage and selection diagnostics for the target and full samples.

findings.title: The claim checker exits successfully while 37 empirical numbers in the new FamilySearch comparison remain unregistered
findings.what_the_code_does: The checker lists uncovered numbers in `unreg`, but its exit condition is only `return 1 if bad or missing else 0`; `unreg` is not part of the failure condition. The committed report consequently records 37 uncovered numbers, including the headline 20.1%, 22.3%, and cell-level comparisons, while the command still reports success.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper’s new comparison with FamilySearch names contains a dense set of headline results that can become stale without making the replication gate fail. This defeats the stated purpose of the claims registry and permits a green run even when an entire results subsection is not checked against generated outputs.
findings.how_to_check: Run `python replication/check_claims.py; echo $LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell. It reports `unregistered result-like numbers in the draft: 37` but returns exit code 0. Then inspect `replication/claims_report.md` from line 112 onward.
findings.suggested_fix: Register the Section 4.3 claims and its three generated exhibits in `replication/claims.toml`, including assertions for the qualitative comparisons at paper lines 659, 686, 688, and 695. Make non-ignored uncovered result-like numbers produce a nonzero exit code.

findings.title: The linkage documentation still reports obsolete truth-dependent results and the old one-sided contradiction definition
findings.what_the_code_does: The documentation says a pair is directly contradicted only when the 1940 record has a different truth partner and reports old values such as HLINK verified counts of 28,357,041 and 28,863,711. Current code checks both census sides, and the regenerated HLINK table reports 28,786,787 and 29,301,006; the ABE/JW documentation likewise retains the pre-rerun counts and recalls.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper tables are correct, but a replicator using the package documentation as expected output will conclude that a successful rerun failed or may implement the obsolete one-sided classification. The same document says the tables have used the complete file since 2026-11-09, making the inconsistency especially misleading.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n "28,357,041|6,222,698|1940 record.*truth set" LINKAGE/DOCUMENTATION.md` and compare those rows with the four files under the paper repository’s `linkage_tables/`.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate or manually synchronize the results section from the current four table outputs, update the restricted denominators and match rates, and define contradiction as either census person having a different truth partner.

verified_clean.item: The active truth-file path is consistent across analysis, preflight, and manifest.
verified_clean.evidence: `$D_TRUTH` points to `truth_from_machineA` at LINKAGE/code/shared/paths.do:93; the machine-B preflight checks the same file at replication/run_machineB.do:65; its hash is recorded at replication/input_manifest_machineB.md:22.

verified_clean.item: The revised paper truth-based counts match the regenerated tables.
verified_clean.evidence: Paper line 107 reports 523,399 and 1,320,314, matching F:/github_repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/figures/deaglan_abe_jw_restricted.tex:15. The current claims checker found 56 registered claims matching and no mismatches.

verified_clean.item: Missing ages are not silently retained by the age thresholds.
verified_clean.evidence: Both table scripts use `keep if age >= 8 & !missing(age)` at LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:45 and LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:189.

verified_clean.item: Blank middle initials cannot inflate the agreement rates.
verified_clean.evidence: The ABE/JW script requires `mi1930 != "" & mi1940 != ""` before equality at LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:228-231; HLINK applies the same guard at LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:374-377.

verified_clean.item: Candidate links are classified against both the 1930 and 1940 truth mappings.
verified_clean.evidence: ABE/JW performs both merges and assigns verified, unverifiable, and contradicted categories at LINKAGE/code/01_abe_jw/linkage_analysis.do:195-203; HLINK mirrors this at LINKAGE/code/02_hlink/linkage_analysis_newlinks.do:341-349.

verified_clean.item: The paper distinguishes transcription agreement from accuracy in its direct model evaluation.
verified_clean.evidence: F:/github_repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:277-305 explicitly calls the metrics agreement with commercial transcriptions, discusses selection toward legible records, and says adjudicated names would be required for accuracy.

review_limits: The external data were not available in the review environment, so the Stata pipeline and the reported row counts, uniqueness assertions, and hashes could not be independently rerun.

The upstream construction of `unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1930.dta` and `unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1940.dta` is not present in the reviewed code. Whether names entered those links—and therefore the exact degree of circularity—could not be established.
The Python claim checker and static syntax checks were runnable; Stata-specific runtime behavior was assessed from source only.

The paper lives in a separate repository. Its current draft includes the FamilySearch-comparison section from an earlier paper commit as well as the truth-rerun changes associated with this code range.
